title: Helionics - Security & Hosting Roadmap Discovery
summary: Introductory discovery covering Helionics' security requirements for LLM inference: SOC2/ISO expectations, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit log retention, KMS options and data residency. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment paths and next steps for a short pilot and security docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
action_items: Maya Patel: Share SOC 2 + ISO artifact summary and compliance whitepaper — due 2026-06-21
Connor Liu: Provide sample architecture diagram for Private VPC deployment and KMS integration — due 2026-06-22
Ria Menon: Send current encryption and key management requirements doc to Redwood — due 2026-06-20
Jordan Swift: Confirm list of sandbox datasets for pilot (no PHI) — due 2026-06-24
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and security deck
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) for private deployment connectivity
Scope 2-week hosted pilot with limited tokens and logging enabled

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-17 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood), Jordan (Helionics Head Infra), Ria (Helionics CISO), Avery (Platform Eng), Diego (Procurement)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be incomplete)
Helionics is evaluating options for serving LLM inference across hosted and private models. Primary concerns: auditability, key management, and ability to integrate with their SSO IdP. They prefer vendor support for SOC2 evidence and an on-prem compatible private control plane.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, account exec for Redwood Inference. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Jordan Swift: Jordan here, hey Maya.
[00:07] Ria Menon: Ria on the line.
[00:09] Avery Cole: Avery, platform.
[00:12] Diego Ramos: Diego from procurement.
[00:14] Connor Liu: Connor, I'll be the engineer today. Samir is also on the chat, behind the scenes.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Great, goal for today is to understand security + hosting constraints, we can cover SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS, data retention, and then outline next steps.
[00:30] Jordan Swift: Sounds good — to give context, Helionics is building document summarization and automated triage tools, none of the workloads have PHI but some internal IP we want protected. We're leaning toward hosted for speed, but ops wants deterministic performance so Dedicated is tempting and Ria is strongly pushing private for compliance.
[00:45] Ria Menon: Yeah, our security team needs clear evidence we can present to auditors — SOC 2 type 2 report, iso 27001 summary, and we also need to know how logs are retained and exported. Also, single sign-on via our IdP (Okta) is required.
[01:05] Connor Liu: Understood. High level — Redwood provides hosted endpoints by default, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private deployment where the control plane sits in your VPC or on-prem. For SOC2/ISO we maintain artifacts and a compliance pack we can share. For SSO, we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC integrations, and RBAC via our enterprise console.
[01:30] Avery Cole: For RBAC, do you have attribute-based rules? We need a least-privilege model so product engineers only have token-level access to call generation endpoints and ops can manage models.
[01:45] Samir Doshi: We do role templates plus custom roles. It's not full ABAC out of the box but we can map SAML attributes to roles and use groups for fine-grained control.
[02:05] Ria Menon: What about audit logs — I need immutable logs with export for SIEM (Splunk) and a retention policy toggle, we may need 7 years for some biz units.
[02:25] Connor Liu: Logs are captured for request metadata, token counts, latency, and model versions. For Hosted we keep detailed logs for N days by default then aggregated metrics; for Dedicated/Private you can configure long-term export to your S3 or push to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder. Immutability depends on your storage backend but we can provide signed audit bundles.
[02:50] Jordan Swift: Signed audit bundles? Can you elaborate, sometimes these vendors hand-wave that.
[02:58] Maya Patel: Yeah, good point. Connor, do you want to explain the audit artifact flow?
[03:03] Connor Liu: Sure. For Dedicated we can enable a write-once storage policy and generate cryptographic hashes for daily log bundles, we provide a manifest and signature. For Private, since it's customer-managed storage, you get full control and we help instrument a signed pipeline. For Hosted we provide certified reports and tailorable export, but long-term signed chain-of-custody is easier with Dedicated/Private.
[03:35] Ria Menon: That helps. Now encryption — we need BYOK and HSM-backed keys. Do you support customer-managed keys in major clouds?
[03:48] Connor Liu: Yes. We support customer-managed KMS across AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can integrate with your HSM/KMS via networked key endpoints. Hosted supports BYOK for data-at-rest and envelope encryption. There are some differences in key rotation and latency when HSM calls are in the loop.
[04:10] Avery Cole: Any impact on inference latency when using external KMS? Our 95th percentile SLO is 200ms in production.
[04:20] Connor Liu: We do envelope encryption so the per-request path doesn't call KMS. KMS is used at key unwrap time during model load and config changes. So runtime token generation isn't impacted by synchronous KMS calls, but startup and scaling operations will have KMS interactions.
[04:40] Jordan Swift: Ok that alleviates the worst case. For data residency — we have EU customers so some workloads must be EU-hosted. What's your region coverage?
[04:53] Maya Patel: We have hosted regions in NA and EU and will expand APAC. Dedicated can be provisioned in the region of your choice, and Private obviously sits in your VPC region. We can ensure data never leaves region for EU-bound workloads.
[05:10] Ria Menon: Contractually we need to see data retention SLAs and the ability to purge logs on demand for GDPR.
[05:18] Samir Doshi: Purge APIs exist for Private/Dedicated where you control storage. For Hosted we offer purge workflows and retention windows, but note that backups and downstream exports may still exist per our retention policy; we can outline contractual language for stricter deletion controls in enterprise agreements.
[05:40] Diego Ramos: From procurement side, we need to understand liability and indemnity around data exfiltration, and whether Redwood will sign a DPA and security addendum.
[05:50] Maya Patel: Yes, we have a standard DPA and security addendum; we'll attach those. For higher risk customers we have bespoke terms.
[06:00] Avery Cole: If we do a pilot, can we do it in Hosted first to move fast and then pivot to Dedicated/Private for production?
[06:10] Connor Liu: That's a common path. Hosted pilot to validate models and perf; Dedicated reserved pools for scale and isolation; Private for the most restrictive compliance. We'll show migration patterns and model pinning so you get consistent API behavior.
[06:25] Jordan Swift: Metrics and cost — how do you provide cost transparency? Token-level breakdowns?
[06:30] Samir Doshi: We expose token usage, per-model cost, per-route breakdowns in the Console and via APIs. For Dedicated we publish effective unit economics after reserved capacity fees. For Private, costs are consumption + infra and we help with a cost-ops spreadsheet.
[06:50] Ria Menon: One technical question — do you persist context/kv cache across restarts? How is that logged?
[06:58] Connor Liu: The KV cache is ephemeral in the runtime; we persist checkpoints for long-running sessions if you opt in. Access to KV cache events are recorded in audit logs as config events, not raw prompt content, for privacy reasons. We also provide tools to scrub sensitive fields.
[07:20] Jordan Swift: Good. Any red flags on data handling we should watch for?
[07:25] Maya Patel: We'll share our security whitepaper. One caveat: when using third-party embeddings or evals, you should understand whether those services receive raw content — we recommend keeping embeddings in-house for sensitive datasets.
[07:40] Ria Menon: About SSO — we run Okta and have SCIM for group sync. Can SCIM provision groups to the Redwood console?
[07:47] Connor Liu: Yes, SCIM is supported for group sync and provisioning. Group mapping can feed RBAC roles and we can map Okta groups to Redwood console roles.
[08:05] Avery Cole: Can we restrict model deployments per team? Ops wants to prevent devs from pulling large models into prod infra.
[08:12] Samir Doshi: You can apply model-level policies and tenant-level quotas; we also have a deployment approval workflow for Dedicated and Private.
[08:30] Diego Ramos: Timeline question — what's a realistic time to get Dedicated provisioned?
[08:36] Maya Patel: Typically 4-8 weeks depending on region and capacity, possibly faster if we use burst pathways. Private on-prem can take longer due to networking. Hosted pilot can start within days.
[08:50] Jordan Swift: Budget is a factor; we need an estimate for a small Dedicated pool vs hosted consumption for expected monthly tokens ~12M tokens.
[08:59] Samir Doshi: We'll put together a cost model for both. For 12M tokens we can show the per-token cost and a committed vs on-demand comparison.
[09:15] Ria Menon: A question on monitoring — do you provide tamper-evident logs and integrations to our SIEM?
[09:22] Connor Liu: Yes, SIEM integration via log-forwarding, signed bundles, and webhook alerts. For tamper evidence we can provide signed manifests and integrate with your object-store immutability features.
[09:40] Jordan Swift: Anything else around regulatory certs? We need ISO 27001 details and whether you have subservice organizations listed.
[09:48] Maya Patel: We'll include our ISO summary and list of sub-processors. For SOC2 we'll provide the report under NDA.
[10:00] Diego Ramos: Great. From procurement I'll need estimated terms and a sample SOW for a pilot.
[10:07] Maya Patel: We'll send a pilot SOW with token caps and logging enabled.
[10:15] Ria Menon: One more technical: for Private deployment, do you maintain a control plane that still phones home, or is it fully self-contained?
[10:23] Connor Liu: The Private offering has an optional air-gapped mode. By default the control plane communicates for updates and support, but in air-gapped mode you operate independently and we provide signed bundles and an offline update mechanism.
[10:40] Avery Cole: That would solve our auditors' concerns.
[10:45] Jordan Swift: Ok let's recap next steps.
[10:48] Maya Patel: Recap: Redwood sends SOC2/ISO artifacts, security deck, sample DPA, pilot SOW and cost model. Helionics shares encryption requirements and sandbox datasets. Schedule SE deep dive for private deployment.
[11:05] Diego Ramos: Sounds good, we'll expect docs by Monday.
[11:10] Maya Patel: I'll get those out today and put the SE deep dive on the calendar for next week. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
